sources.ref: Crinacle EQ tool: gain slider from -15 to +15 dB

Walkplay Android app 2.3.1 (com.ttgk.musicbox): its product catalog (data/catalogs/walkplay.json) lists 0x3302:0xc20f "Protocol Micro" under scheme 11; band count, filter types and Q and pre-gain limits as the app's editor gives them for that scheme

meta.notes:
Guided read with the eqcaps inspector on 2026-10-03 in peq.szwalkplay.com: its buttons move gain and Q by 0.1, but typed values reach the device as they are, rounded onto the 1/256 wire grid, so the steps are 0.00390625 (the evidence file's own summary, 0.01, predates that reading; INSPECTOR §3.3). Bands 2–7 not checked: assumed to match band 1.
peq.szwalkplay.com caps gain at ±10 dB; the Crinacle EQ tool allows ±15.
MIC Offset: written as s16 ×256 dB; the device rounds what it's sent to the nearest 1.5 dB from -15 to +15 and reads that back (every whole and half dB from -15 to +15 written and read back on 2026-10-31, firmware 0.2). peq.szwalkplay.com (scheme 11) shows a slider from -15 to +15 in whole steps and sends its value + 0.5 dB, so the device holds the grid point nearest to that; NICEHCK's app calls the same field dB. The app's Save sends [1,1,0]; the handler doesn't send it after a control write, and whether an unsaved change survives a replug is untested.
Walkplay's Android app (2.3.1) lists this device under scheme 11, with the same 8 bands of peaking, low shelf, low pass and high pass filters that the 2026-10-03 read found. The read-back of 2026-10-03 is where walkplay-app's Q and pre-gain limits come from: the device held Q from 0.1015625 up to 10 and a pre-gain from -16 to +6 dB in whole dB, as peq.szwalkplay.com offers, which is wider than the Android app's editor (Q to 5, pre-gain -8 to +4). Only the gain range (±15) is this profile's own.
